build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

exclude: not module 4: the stream's zero padding and the sector filler after its last packed byte (input byte 1424 of its stream, from T33/L3 byte 155 on side 4), decoded as $00 until the unpacker's $D000 limit; nothing reads them

comments.text: Module 4: the destruction of Base Cochise, the game's ending. Entry, called by the game's JSR $CA00 ($884E) after load_module ($03BF) with A = 4. The only code that asks for module 4 is the self-destruct countdown: game $82B5 (from the main loop, $7ED2) does LDA #$84 / JMP $8845 once $F4F9 is set and the elapsed-time count $04-$06 is $F0 or more past $F4FA-$F4FC, which map 20's code at $406B stores when it arms the countdown ($F0 units of 15 game seconds: one hour, by map 20's clock at $408B); no map square's record holds $84. Writes the current map back (save_map), then sets bit 0 of byte +$4B of every character record 1 to $0A (the radio program reads it, $7EC9). Then: the explosion ($CA1E), the parties caught in the base ($CA69), the hilltop scene ($CB19), the closing text ($CB89) and the return to play ($CBBA). Returns carry set when a party is left, so the game redraws ($8872, $AC8C); carry clear when none is, and the main loop then finds $0A = 0 and runs the death program ($7ED5).

Operand of the LDA #imm at $CA13, the counter of the flag loop at the top of cochise_destruction: the record number, 1 up to $0A, whose byte +$4B gets bit 0 set; stored at $CA05, where select_character ($0338) also points $66/$67 at that record.

The explosion: keeps $AB and $AC (the picture number and the animation flag) on the stack until $CC0B, opens the picture window ($037D), turns animation channel 1 off ($5BFC = 0), loads and starts picture 0 (Base Cochise's dome among mountains; load_m4_picture) and prints the caption '  Cochise  ' (cochise_caption) at column 1, row 13 under it. Then waits 12 rounds of delay_x ($0237), 15 steps of animated_wait, shakes the screen ($044C), waits 45 steps, turns channel 0 off and channel 1 on, prints message 1 (four screens of the base blowing up, each closed by a (RETURN) prompt) and turns channel 0 on.

The parties caught in the blast: keeps the current party $08 in saved_party, clears blast_victims and walks the parties 0 to $0B. A party whose map (party table +$0A) is $10-$14, the five maps of Base Cochise (16, the ground and the dome outside, and 17-20, the levels inside), dies: the location name $F4D0 is emptied, picture 1 (a dark figure against a white glare) is shown, and until the party is empty ($07 = 0) member 1 has CON (+$1D/+$1E) set to 0, message 2 '<name> was killed in the blast.' is printed, blast_victims goes up by one, remove_member ($02C6) takes it out and message 7 prompts and opens a fresh text window. The party's table is then deleted: unless it is the last party ($0B), the tables after it move down 14 bytes ($CAD7-$CAFE); table 3 is cleared ($CC85), $0B drops by one and the same party number is looked at again; saved_party follows the renumbering, $FF when it was the party destroyed. No party left at all ($0B negative) ends the walk.

Operand of the LDY #imm at $CAE7: the offset, from the table at ($68) being overwritten, of the byte copied next, $1B down to $0E, which is the following party's 14-byte table (set at $CADF, stepped down at $CAEF).
Operand of the LDY #imm at $CAEB: where that byte goes, offset $0D down to 0 of the table at ($68) itself (set at $CAE4, stepped down at $CAF2): party table n takes the bytes of table n + 1.

Operand of the LDA #imm at $CAF7: the party table being overwritten by the next one, from the destroyed party up to 3 (stored at $CAD7). For party 3 the bytes come from the 14 after the four tables, $F438-$F445, and table 3 is cleared straight after ($CB00).

The hilltop scene, only when characters are left ($0A not 0): a frame over the map and text windows (open_hilltop_frame), the Geiger gauge drawn dark ($9F = $FF, $04E1), side 4 asked for and two pages read raw from its track 3, logical sector 4 to $3400-$35FF ($03B0): 64 glyphs that draw a vertical 'WASTELAND' logo. They are swapped in for the font's glyphs $20-$5F (swap_font_glyphs), printed four to a row in colour $86 from column 33, rows 1-16 (window left edge 33, bottom line $C0 for the while), the font is swapped back, and picture 2 (a ranger with a rifle on a hilltop, the base burning below) is shown beside the logo (load_m4_picture, X = 2).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $CB62: the glyph code printed next in the logo, $20 up to $5F (set at $CB58, stepped at $CB67; $60 ends the loop at $CB77).

The closing text. With characters left it goes in the message area under the hilltop scene: message 6 (the source, The History of the Rangers, Vol. II, by Karl Allard, 2095), 4 (the rangers watching from a neighbouring hilltop), 5 (the malignant creature burning in the pyre) and, when blast_victims is not 0, 3 (the rangers who gave their lives); then message 8 '(RETURN)' and a key ($022F, after clearing $EC). With none left it goes in the text window: messages 6, 7 (prompt, fresh window), 3 and 7.

Operand of the LDA #imm at $CB9C: the number of characters killed in the blast, 0 at $CA70 and one more at each death ($CAAB). When it is 0 the closing text skips message 3, the epitaph for the rangers who died.

Back to play: clears the countdown flag $F4F9 (so game $82B5 stays quiet), makes saved_party the current party (party 0 when that party died), marks no map in memory ($91 = $FF: $3400 holds pictures now), enters the world map (map 0, $03B6) and makes its square at column 2, row 3 class 4, number 2 ($0434): the record ($4D50 in map 0) whose message is 'The debris littered here is the fireblackened ruins of Base Cochise.' and whose tile is $2B, the broken dome (the world map as stored has record 1 there, drawn as desert, tile $20); then writes the world map back. Takes the current party's column, row and map from its table (+8, +9, +$0A) into $57/$58, $02/$03 (less $59/$5A) and $09, restores $AB/$AC and clears the message area ($0320). With no party left ($0B negative) returns carry clear; otherwise enters the party's map again with $91 = $FF, unpacks its stream once more ($03C5, which enter_map has just done) and returns carry set.
Logo glyphs still to print on the current row, 4 down to 1 (set at $CB5F, counted down at $CB6A); at 0 a new line ($CB6F).

saved_party: the party current when the blast began ($08, stored at $CA6B). Lowered by one when an earlier party's table is deleted ($CAC5), $FF when that party itself died ($CACC); made current again at $CBBF, party 0 when it is $FF.
Inner counter of animated_wait: read_key polls left in the current step, 64 down to 1 (set at $CC34, counted down at $CC3A).

Shows message A of module 4's text (show_m4_message) and goes on into if_none_left: when no character is left a (RETURN) prompt and a fresh text window follow, carry set. Used for messages 4, 5 and 6 of the closing text.

animated_wait: X steps of 64 calls of read_key ($022A). Each call runs one tick of the picture animation ($05C5), which lets one call in 512 through to the animation channels, and a key pressed meanwhile is taken and dropped. Returns X = 0. Called with X = 15 ($CA49) and 45 ($CA51), around the screen shake.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $CC3F: animated_wait's outer count, the steps of 64 polls still to go; stored on entry and again after each step ($CC2F).

Prints message A of module 4's text block ($CD56) with print_message ($0311), word-wrapped ($0302), through the current output: $43/$44 = $CD56. Used for the explosion, each death and the prompts (messages 1, 2 and 7), and by show_m4_message when no character is left.

Shows message A of module 4's text. When characters are left ($0A not 0): in the message area at the foot of the screen through show_map_message ($031D), with $61/$62 pointed at m4_text_header for the call so that the map's text block is the module's, then put back. When none is: print_m4_message, in the text window.

m4_text_header: a stand-in map header of one word, $CD56, module 4's text block. show_m4_message points $61/$62 here so that show_map_message, which takes the text block from the header's first word (select_map_text, $1E4F), shows the module's messages in the message area.

if_none_left: when characters are left ($0A not 0) returns carry clear at once. When none is, prints message 7 ({06}{07}: the (RETURN) prompt, then a fresh text window) and returns carry set; the closing text uses the carry to skip its last '(RETURN)' ($CBA8).
Zeroes the 14 bytes of party table A ($029F points $68/$69 at $F400 + 14 * A). Used on table 3 after a destroyed party's table has been deleted ($CB02).

load_m4_picture: loads picture X (0-2) of module 4 to $3400, the map's memory (the map was written back at $CA00), and starts it. Keeps X in picture_index, asks for side 4 ($02DB), stops the animation ($AC = 0), reads the sector at track picture_tracks[X], logical sector picture_sectors[X] to $5A00 ($FD19) and unpacks from its byte 0 ($04F3) with $CE = picture_stream_pages[X] and the limit $3400 + picture_buffer_pages[X] pages ($CC/$CD; $B9/$BA = $3400). For picture 2 the area's last column, header byte 2, becomes $20 (32), so that the picture stops left of the logo at columns 33-36. Then the animation on ($AC = 1), $C5 = 1 (the animation tick no longer reloads picture $AB over this one, $05C9) and start_picture ($041F).
Operand of the LDX #imm at $CCC0: the picture being loaded, 0-2, stored at $CC92 and read again at $CC9E and $CCD0 (picture 2 gets its last column cut to 32).
picture_tracks: the track of each module-4 picture's first sector on side 4, pictures 0-2: 3, 2, 1. Read at $CCA6 into $10.

picture_sectors: the logical sector of each picture's first sector: 2, 12, 20 (read at $CCA1 into $11). The streams run on down the logical sectors, picture 0 into track 2 from its sector 20; track 3's sectors 4 and 3, just before picture 0, hold the two raw pages of the logo ($CB34).
picture_stream_pages: $CE for each picture's unpack, 11, 13, 13: the input pages the unpacker may read before it stops (read at $CCC2).
picture_buffer_pages: how many pages from $3400 each picture may fill, the unpack limit $CD: 14, 17, 16 (to $41FF, $44FF and $43FF; read at $CCB5).

open_hilltop_frame: frames the area over the map and text windows for the hilltop scene, draw_frame ($0398) from column 0, row 0 to column 37, row 17 (right edge $26 = 39 meanwhile; the 38 stored in $25 at $CCF3 is overwritten at $CCFD), then clears the inside, columns 1-36, pixel lines 8-135 ($27 = 8, $28 = $87), in colour $86 ($025C). The window is left at those columns and lines; $EB is kept.

swap_font_glyphs: exchanges the font's glyphs $20-$5F ($C600-$C7FF) with the 512 bytes at $3400-$35FF, byte for byte. Called once to put the logo's glyphs into the font and once to put the font back ($CB47, $CB81).
cochise_caption: '  Cochise  ' and a zero byte, in the font's ASCII order: the caption printed under the explosion picture at column 1, row 13 ($CA3F), where the location's name usually goes.

m4_text_block: module 4's packed text, in the format of every text block (5-bit codes through the alphabet, groups of four messages; $43/$44 at $CC4A, and m4_text_header). This is its 60-byte alphabet, codes 0-$3B: ' etraoishnldugcypmb', new line, ',wf.', end, 'vk"', {07}, {06}, 'x0z9521)(', apostrophe, '$', {0B}, {08}, then $7F for the codes it leaves unused ($2B-$3B).
m4_text_groups: the text block's three group offsets, relative to $CD92: $0006, $0139, $025B, so group 0 (messages 0-3) at $CD98, group 1 (4-7) at $CECB and group 2 (8 on) at $CFED.

Group 0 of module 4's text. Message 0 is empty (an end code in bits 0-4 of $CD98, never printed); message 1 runs from bit 5 of $CD98 to $CE58: '{07}Shuddering explosions rock the base, fire blossoms throughout every doorway.
{06}{07}Everywhere walls and supports buckle and crumble in the explosions.
{06}{07}Debris and shrapnel fly everywhere killing everything it touches.
{06}{07}You can almost imagine robots screaming as they realize they, too, are mortal.
{06}{07}' ({07} opens a fresh text window, {06} is the (RETURN) prompt). Printed at $CA5F.
Message 2, from bit 4 of $CE58: '\n{0B} was killed in the blast.\n' ({0B} prints the current character's name); once for each character who dies in the base ($CAA8).

Message 3, from bit 2 of $CE6B to $CECA: '\n  "But certainly most important of all were the rangers who gave their lives to destroy Base Cochise, the greatest threat that man has ever known."\n'. Printed when anyone died in the blast, or when no character is left ($CBA0).

Group 1 (messages 4-7) begins here. Message 4: '\n  "High on a neighboring hilltop, shielded from the explosion's full fury, the rangers watched as fire and ruin claimed Base Cochise."\n'; only when characters are left ($CB92).

Message 5, from bit 6 of $CF23: '"Deep in their hearts they knew that in that hideous pyre burned the malignant creature that almost ended all life on earth."\n'; only when characters are left ($CB97).

Message 6, from bit 6 of $CF73 to $CFEA: '\nThe following is an excerpt from the dedication to The History of the Rangers, Vol. II, by Karl Allard, 2095, Allard Press, Desert Center, Hardbound pp ii, $10 gold.\n'. The first message of the closing text in both endings ($CB89).
The rest of message 6, from the 'ngers' of 'Rangers' on. Nothing reads $CFA4 as such: the engine's BIT $CFA4 at $1627 is a skip that hides LDY $CF, which is why the disassembler names this address.

Message 7, from bit 4 of $CFEA to $CFEC: '{06}{07}', the (RETURN) prompt and then a fresh text window; after each death ($CAB5) and in if_none_left ($CC7E). Bits 3-7 of $CFEC are unused: the next group starts on a byte.

Group 2 begins here; message 8, to bit 3 of $CFF9: '\n(RETURN){08}' ({08} draws the word-wrap buffer), the last line of the ending when characters are left ($CBAA), after which a key is awaited. The group table promises messages 9-11 as well, but the module prints none of them.

$20, the last byte of module 4's packed data: in the stream (side 4, track 33, logical sector 3 from byte 155) it is a table code, '1' and '000', for entry 0 of the stream's table ($20), in bits 4-1 of input byte 1424 ($90), the last non-zero byte. Nothing reads it: message 8, the last the module prints, ends in bit 3 of $CFF9 (bits 4-7 are 0), and the text decoder fetches a byte only when it needs a bit. $CFFB-$CFFF are $00 decoded from the zero padding after it (bit 0 of byte 1424, then the filler from byte 1425) until the unpacker stops at $D000.
